solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: European film, major work (4)

blocks.note: a pic is a film, short for picture

annotation.surface: A listing for a European film billed as a major work.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma makes "European film" look like one phrase describing the major work; in fact it splits into two separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: An epic is a long, ambitious work such as a poem or film.

entries.clue: Beat or bean perhaps (5)

blocks.note: the regular throb of blood you feel at the wrist
the family of edible seeds that includes beans, peas and lentils

annotation.surface: Someone unsure whether a thing is a beat or a bean.
annotation.walkthrough: PULSE covers both the heartbeat at your wrist and the dried seeds of beans and lentils; "perhaps" signals that a bean is only one example.
annotation.definitionFit: A pulse is both a rhythmic beat and an edible legume seed.

entries.clue: Type of TV studio cleric condemned, following Conservative’s lead (6-7)

indicatorNotes.condemned: the studio cleric is damned, so his letters are wrecked
indicatorNotes.following: the anagram comes after the C
indicatorNotes.lead: the lead of a word is its first letter

annotation.surface: A television studio's resident cleric has been condemned, trailing a Conservative politician.
annotation.walkthrough: "TV studio" reads as one phrase, but TV belongs to the definition and "studio" to the fodder; the break is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: Closed-circuit TV is a private camera system not broadcast to the public, as in security cameras.

entries.clue: Hero‘s receding US hairstyle – Yank at heart (8)

indicatorNotes.receding: something receding goes backwards, so US turns round
indicatorNotes.at heart: the heart of a word is its middle

blocks.note: a perm is a curled hairstyle
the middle two letters of yANk

annotation.surface: An American with a receding hairline and a hairstyle to match.
annotation.walkthrough: "Receding" sits beside "hairstyle" to suggest a hairline; it is working on US instead.
annotation.definitionFit: Superman is the archetypal comic-book hero.

entries.clue: Maybe halve quiet area, the last to go (5)

indicatorNotes.the last to go: the last letter of AREA is dropped

annotation.surface: A planner thinking of halving a quiet area and shedding its far end.
annotation.walkthrough: "Maybe" makes the definition fair: halving is one way to share, not the only one.
annotation.definitionFit: To halve something between two people is one way of sharing it.

entries.clue: Delighted, extremely proud about legal agreement (7)

indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters
indicatorNotes.about: the outer letters go around LEASE

blocks.note: the first and last letters of ProuD
a lease is a legal agreement to rent

annotation.surface: Someone delighted and very proud about a signed legal agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: "Extremely proud" reads as "very proud"; here "extremely" asks for proud's outermost letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Pleased and delighted both mean happy with something.

entries.clue: Outrageous neck – hold court without interruption (5-3-5)

indicatorNotes.Outrageous: the letters behave wildly and are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone with outrageous neck, meaning cheek, who holds court and talks on and on.
annotation.walkthrough: "Neck" is British slang for cheek or nerve, so the surface is a brazen talker; none of it is the definition except the last two words.
annotation.definitionFit: Round-the-clock means continuing day and night without a break.

entries.clue: Female relative welcoming exotic gem’s boost (7)

indicatorNotes.welcoming: AUNT takes the other letters in
indicatorNotes.exotic: the letters of GEM turn strange, so they are rearranged

blocks.note: an aunt is a female relative

annotation.surface: An aunt is pleased when she receives an exotic jewel.
annotation.walkthrough: "Welcoming" looks like the aunt's warm greeting; it is the instruction to take letters inside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: boosting a figure and augmenting it both mean making it bigger.

entries.clue: Distribute everything on cue at the event, to begin with (8)

indicatorNotes.to begin with: take what each word begins with, its first letter

blocks.clueFragment: on cue at the event, to begin with
blocks.note: the first letters of On Cue At The Event

annotation.surface: An organiser handing everything out on cue at the start of an event.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cue" suggests a stage prompt; here it only lends its first letter to the run of initials.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: handing out portions of a budget or resource is distributing it.

entries.clue: Press for outrigger to be used regularly (4)

indicatorNotes.used regularly: only letters at regular intervals are used

annotation.surface: Pressing for an outrigger canoe to be put to regular use.
annotation.walkthrough: "Press" can look like a newspaper or a machine; here it is the verb, to press someone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: pressing someone to act is the same push as urging them.

entries.clue: Reportedly plant again and withdraw (6)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: what is reported is heard, so the sound counts

blocks.note: to reseed is to plant again

annotation.surface: A gardener replanting a bed and then stepping back.
annotation.walkthrough: The two words are spelt differently but sound the same; a homophone only needs matching sounds.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: floodwaters or hairlines withdraw when they move back.

entries.clue: Section of memoir I briefly make fun of (3)

indicatorNotes.Section of: the answer is a section cut from the words that follow

annotation.surface: A writer who briefly pokes fun at themselves in part of their memoir.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across two word breaks, from the end of "memoir" through "I" into the start of "briefly".
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: teasing someone good-naturedly is ribbing them.

entries.clue: Waterlogged turf beside lair (6)

indicatorNotes.beside: DEN is placed next to SOD

blocks.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is an animal's lair

annotation.surface: Soaking wet turf lying next to an animal's lair.
annotation.walkthrough: Sod here is the grass-and-soil sense, not the British insult.
annotation.definitionFit: Sodden means soaked through, waterlogged.

entries.clue: Easy to see they’re chess players (5-3-5)

blocks.note: said of an issue that is clear-cut, with no grey areas
the two sides in chess are named after the colours of their pieces

annotation.surface: An observation that you can easily spot who is playing chess.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer is both the clear-cut, no-grey-areas sense and the names of the two chess sides.
annotation.definitionFit: Something black-and-white is clear-cut, with no grey areas.

entries.clue: Fuss about English skin product? (7)

indicatorNotes.about: about means around, so LATHER is placed around E

blocks.note: to be in a lather is to be in a fuss

annotation.surface: A fuss about some English skincare product.
annotation.walkthrough: "Skin product" suggests a cream; the question mark flags that it means something made from an animal's skin.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: tanned hide is a product made from skin, and the question mark flags the twist.

entries.clue: Football team, first-class, learns afresh (7)

indicatorNotes.afresh: the letters of LEARNS are laid out anew

blocks.note: A = first-class, as in A1 or grade A

annotation.surface: A top football team that relearns its game.
annotation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London Premier League football club.
annotation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a well-known English football team.

entries.clue: Observer I picked up (3)

indicatorNotes.picked up: what is picked up is heard

blocks.note: the letter I, said out loud, is the organ of sight

annotation.surface: A spy noting that he has been spotted.
annotation.walkthrough: The pronoun I and the organ of sight sound identical.
annotation.definitionFit: An eye observes; a private eye is also an observer.

entries.clue: Sign fellow’s abandoning thesaurus (6)

indicatorNotes.abandoning: to abandon is to leave behind, so HES is left out of the word

annotation.surface: A man signing that he is giving up his thesaurus.
annotation.walkthrough: "Fellow's" is read as "he's", and those letters come out of the book of synonyms.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword sense: a sign is a star sign, and the bull is one of the twelve.

entries.clue: Blame Bill, copper? Snide, beginning and end (6)

indicatorNotes.beginning and end: take the first and last letters of snide

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the first and last letters of SnidE

annotation.surface: Blaming a snide policeman called Bill.
annotation.walkthrough: The Old Bill are the police in Britain, so "Bill, copper" reads as one police officer; the two words work separately.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to blame someone for a wrong is to charge them with it.

entries.clue: Player seen in factory (5)

indicatorNotes.seen in: the answer can be seen inside the next word

annotation.surface: A performer spotted on a factory floor.
annotation.walkthrough: "Player" suggests sport or games; here it means someone who plays a role on stage.
annotation.definitionFit: A player is an actor, one who plays a part.

entries.clue: Military action, for example, close to castle is set up (5)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its final letter
indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, set up means written upwards, so reversed

annotation.surface: A military assault near a castle being prepared.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole string is built in clue order and then turned upwards, since this is a down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A siege is a military operation surrounding a stronghold.

entries.clue: Second person, old, lodged in guest house (4)

indicatorNotes.lodged in: the answer lodges inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A second guest, elderly, staying at a boarding house.
annotation.walkthrough: "Second person" is grammar: the old second-person singular pronoun, with "old" saying it is archaic.
annotation.definitionFit: Thou is the archaic form of "you", the second-person pronoun.

entries.clue: Element of intro wrong: information to follow (8)

indicatorNotes.to follow: to follow is to come after, so GEN is placed after the anagram

blocks.note: gen = information, as in "get the gen on"

annotation.surface: A presenter finds part of the introduction wrong, with more facts still to come.
annotation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information; "Element of" reads as "part of" in the surface but the definition is "Element" alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the gas making up most of the air is one of the chemical elements.

entries.clue: At back, chap, snake, one not worth listening to (8)

indicatorNotes.At back: the back of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: A man at the back with a snake, whom nobody bothers to hear.
annotation.walkthrough: "Chap" wants to be a whole man; "At back" takes only its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: someone who chatters on foolishly is not worth listening to.

entries.clue: Was familiar with novel, by the sound of it (4)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: judged by its sound, not its spelling

annotation.surface: Someone who seemed to know a particular novel.
annotation.walkthrough: "Novel" wants to be a book; it is the adjective meaning new.
annotation.definitionFit: Knew is the past tense of know, to be familiar with.
